record.original_question: Let C:f=0 be a line arrangement in P^2 and let E_C=T⟨C⟩(-1) be the associated rank-2 logarithmic vector bundle. If (d_1^{L_0}, d_2^{L_0}) denotes the splitting type of E_C along a generic line L_0 in P^2, is this generic splitting type determined by the combinatorics of the arrangement?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $C:f=0$ be a line arrangement in the complex projective plane $\mathbb{P}^2$, where $f \in \mathbb{C}[x,y,z]$ is a reduced homogeneous polynomial whose irreducible factors are linear forms. Let $T\langle C\rangle \subset T_{\mathbb{P}^2}$ denote the sheaf of logarithmic vector fields tangent to $C$, and set
$$E_C := T\langle C\rangle(-1),$$
a rank-2 vector bundle on $\mathbb{P}^2$. For a generic line $L_0 \subset \mathbb{P}^2$, the restriction $E_C|_{L_0}$ splits, by Grothendieck's theorem, as
$$E_C|_{L_0} \cong \mathcal{O}_{L_0}(-d_1^{L_0}) \oplus \mathcal{O}_{L_0}(-d_2^{L_0})$$
for a unique pair of integers $d_1^{L_0} \le d_2^{L_0}$, called the generic splitting type of $E_C$. 

Two line arrangements are said to have the same combinatorics if there is a bijection between their sets of lines preserving the intersection lattice (equivalently, the same matroid / incidence data of multiple points).

Question: Is the generic splitting type $(d_1^{L_0}, d_2^{L_0})$ of $E_C$ determined by the combinatorics of the line arrangement $C$? That is, do any two line arrangements with isomorphic intersection lattices have the same generic splitting type?
artifact.category_tag: logarithmic vector bundles of line arrangements
artifact.status_search_result: The question is stated as a conjecture concerning whether the generic splitting type of the rank-2 logarithmic bundle of a line arrangement is a combinatorial invariant. Related results establish partial cases (e.g., for arrangements with a line containing few intersection points, and for nearly free/free arrangements where splitting types relate to total Tjurina number), but no general proof or counterexample has been reported. The problem is closely related to (and weaker than) Terao's freeness conjecture, which itself remains open.

status_evidence.title: On the splitting types of bundles of logarithmic vector fields along plane curves
status_evidence.snippet: Formula relating Tjurina number and generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle, with applications to free/nearly free arrangements.
status_evidence.claim: Generic splitting type is studied as an invariant, with combinatorial determination known only in special cases.

status_evidence.title: Invariants of combinatorial line arrangements and Rybnikov's example
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of which invariants of line arrangements are combinatorial.
status_evidence.claim: Combinatorial determination of various algebraic invariants of line arrangements remains an active open problem.
